_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. Autumn, and the Pacific is lining up storms like boxcars on a siding. This week you put it all together and follow one storm from start to finish: barometer, wind, and every cloud from the first cirrus to the last shower.

replies.say: The workbook has a chapter on radar.
replies.back: Some fellow’s notion for the future, I expect. Read it anyway.

turns.them: By the end you should read a storm two days off. Questions at the end.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions. Sky, barometer and wind together this time.
That’s a whole storm read. One more lesson, for the winter.
